issues.legal_issue: A conspiracy to commit murder cannot be established from suspicious circumstances alone when there is no reliable evidence that the alleged conspirators agreed or planned to commit the offence.
material_facts: The prosecution alleged that three accused arranged to be imprisoned before the killings to create an alibi and conspired with others to commit the offence.
The alleged conspirators were in custody on the date of the killings after being convicted for travelling without tickets.
One accused had deposited a licensed gun with an arms dealer, but the licence had already been suspended.
The court found no evidence that the alleged conspirators discussed or planned the offence, or arranged their ticketless travel and arrest as part of a plan.
issues.conclusion: The circumstances created suspicion but did not prove a conspiracy; the High Court rightly set aside the conspiracy convictions.
issues.legal_principle: The prosecution must establish guilt by legal proof; suspicion, however strong, cannot substitute for proof. The court applied this principle to the charges under Sections 109 and 120(B) of the Indian Penal Code, read with Section 302, and relied on no earlier case for this issue.

predicates.state_appeal_from_acquittal: The prosecution appealed from an acquittal or from the setting aside of a conviction.
predicates.alleged_conspirators_were_in_custody_dur: The persons alleged to have agreed to commit the offence were in custody when it occurred.
predicates.suspicious_circumstances_were_only_evide: The prosecution relied on circumstances capable of creating suspicion but not independently establishing an agreement to commit the offence.
predicates.no_reliable_evidence_of_planning: The prosecution produced no reliable evidence that the alleged conspirators discussed or planned the offence.

issues.definition: When the prosecution appeal concerns alleged conspirators who were in custody during the offence and the evidence of agreement consists only of suspicious circumstances or lacks reliable proof of planning, the conspiracy is not proved beyond reasonable doubt.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction cannot be sustained on eyewitness evidence that is materially unreliable and so mixed with falsehood that the reliable parts cannot be separated without reconstructing the prosecution case.
material_facts: The prosecution witnesses were closely connected with one faction and had reason to be hostile to the opposing faction.
The earliest complaint falsely attributed participation to persons shown to have been in prison at the time of the offence.
The eyewitness accounts contained material infirmities and contradictions; the injured witnesses were examined medically after a substantial delay, and one had serious visual impairment.
The court found the evidence as a whole unworthy of credence and inextricably mixed with falsehood; one accused, unlike the others, admitted being present at the scene.
The prosecution relied on the number and brutality of the killings, but the court found those circumstances could not replace reliable proof.
issues.conclusion: The prosecution failed to prove the charges beyond reasonable doubt against the accused whose guilt depended on the unreliable evidence; the High Court's acquittals and setting aside of convictions were not to be disturbed. The court noted the exception of the accused who admitted his presence.
issues.legal_principle: The prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt, and the gravity or multiplicity of the offences cannot make unreliable evidence sufficient. Under the principle in Balaka Singh & Ors. v. State of Punjab, [1975] 4 SCC 511, a court may separate truth from falsehood only when the two are separable; where they are inextricably mixed, it cannot reconstruct a new prosecution case by extracting selected details.

rule.if: state_appeal_from_acquittal and material_witnesses_falsely_implicated_persons_shown_absent and evidence_was_inextricably_mixed_with_falsehood and (eyewitness_accounts_had_material_infirmities or corroboration_was_unreliable)

predicates.state_appeal_from_acquittal: The prosecution appealed from an acquittal or from the setting aside of a conviction.
predicates.material_witnesses_falsely_implicated_pe: Prosecution witnesses attributed participation to persons who were shown to be absent from the scene because they were in custody.
predicates.evidence_was_inextricably_mixed_with_fal: The prosecution evidence combined asserted facts and falsehoods in a way that did not permit the reliable parts to be separated without rebuilding the prosecution case.
predicates.eyewitness_accounts_had_material_infirmi: The eyewitness accounts contained material contradictions, credibility problems, or other serious infirmities.
predicates.corroboration_was_unreliable: The evidence offered to support the eyewitness accounts was itself unreliable.

issues.definition: If a prosecution appeal concerns evidence that falsely implicates persons shown to be absent, is inseparable from falsehood, and also has material eyewitness infirmities or unreliable corroboration, guilt is not proved beyond reasonable doubt.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court will not disturb a High Court's acquittal assessment in a State appeal under special leave when the High Court has given record-based reasons and its conclusion is neither perverse nor unreasonable.
material_facts: The State challenged the High Court's decision acquitting accused persons or setting aside their convictions.
The High Court examined the evidence and gave reasons for disbelieving the eyewitnesses and rejecting the prosecution case.
The Supreme Court found those reasons reasonable and the High Court's assessment neither perverse nor unreasonable.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court declined to interfere with the High Court's judgment and dismissed the State's appeals.
issues.legal_principle: In exercising jurisdiction under Article 136 of the Constitution in the appeals before it, the Court found no basis to displace a High Court assessment that was neither perverse nor unreasonable. The judgment relies on no earlier case for this appellate conclusion.

predicates.state_special_leave_appeal_from_high_cou: The State sought special leave to challenge a High Court judgment acquitting accused persons or setting aside their convictions.
predicates.high_court_gave_record_based_reasons: The High Court examined the evidence and explained its reasons for its conclusion.
predicates.high_court_conclusion_was_not_perverse_o: The High Court's conclusion was supported by its assessment of the record and was neither perverse nor unreasonable.

issues.definition: When the State seeks special leave to challenge a High Court acquittal, and the High Court has given record-based reasons for a conclusion that is neither perverse nor unreasonable, the Supreme Court does not interfere with the acquittal.
